RSD03382 is a specific laboratory test code used within the Danish healthcare system's laboratory database to identify measurements of p-thyrotropin, also known as [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] [^src1]. This code plays a critical role in the national quality assurance framework for cardiology, specifically within the "Atrieflimren i Danmark" (Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark) program managed by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1]. 

In the context of monitoring and evaluating the treatment quality for patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, RSD03382 is utilized as part of the technical definitions for Quality Indicator 3 [^src1]. By tracking this specific code alongside a broader panel of laboratory identifiers (such as NPU and ASS codes), healthcare registries can accurately extract data regarding thyroid function testing, which is a vital step in the clinical assessment and management of atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. The documentation of this code serves as a technical reference for implementing register-based analyses and ensuring standardized quality measurement across the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
